articles.title: Death anxiety is linked to worse insomnia through more severe nightmares
articles.summary: Is the fear of death keeping you awake? Recent research suggests that intense death anxiety predicts stronger insomnia symptoms, a link partially explained by a rise in severe nightmares.

articles.title: People who feel lonely show altered brain activity when processing internal physical signals
articles.summary: A recent study indicates that loneliness alters how we perceive internal physical signals. Lonely individuals tend to distrust their bodily sensations and show reduced brain responses to their heartbeats, offering a physiological explanation for the distress of isolation.

articles.title: Brain signals help reproductive cells survive heat stress, new worm study suggests
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a hidden communication network in worms where the nervous system uses small RNA molecules to protect fertility. This shows that an animal's sensory perception can physically buffer its reproductive system against extreme heat.

articles.title: Experts say blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
articles.summary: A new report suggests that blood pressure may be controlled more effectively by increasing potassium while also cutting sodium. Potassium-rich foods can help balance sodium’s effects, but most people consume far less potassium than recommended.

articles.title: Past interpersonal trauma can shape current relationship conflict tactics
articles.summary: How people manage disagreements with romantic partners relies heavily on their attachment orientation. A recent study reveals that individuals with insecure attachments are less likely to compromise and more prone to confrontational or submissive behaviors during relationship disputes.

articles.title: Two new compounds could reveal hidden drivers of Alzheimer’s disease
articles.summary: Vanderbilt researchers created the first selective compound designed to inhibit TAOK-1, a poorly understood protein connected to Alzheimer’s disease. They also discovered a second compound that activates the entire TAOK protein family, offering scientists an unexpected new research tool. Together, the compounds could reveal hidden disease mechanisms and point toward new treatment strategies.

articles.title: Scientists may have found aging’s hidden trigger for brain disease
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a molecular switch that may help explain why aging makes the brain more vulnerable to diseases such as ALS and Huntington’s. In worms, the protein EPS8 builds up with age and triggers signaling that encourages toxic proteins to clump together, damaging neurons and shortening lifespan. Reducing EPS8 activity prevented these harmful aggregates and preserved nerve function.

articles.title: Energy Efficiency of Locally Deployed LLMs: A Preliminary Quantitative GPU Power Benchmark on Consumer Hardware
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.00008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local deployment of large language models (LLMs) is gaining traction due to privacy concerns and the desire for on-premise inference.
